title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 64 (Consequences of rescission of voidable contract)

content.overview: Section 64 provides that when a person at whose option a contract is voidable rescinds it, the other party thereto need not perform any promise therein contained in which he is promisor. The party rescinding a voidable contract shall, if he has received any benefit thereunder from another party to such contract, restore such benefit, so far as may be, to the person from whom it was received.
content.glance: Rescission of voidable contract → other party need not perform; rescinding party must restore benefit received so far as may be.
content.study: When a party entitled to avoid a voidable contract rescinds it, the other party need not perform any promise in which he is promisor. The rescinding party must restore any benefit received under the contract, so far as may be, to the person from whom it was received. Current-law framing: establish valid rescission of a voidable contract; apply non-performance by the other party; apply restoration of benefit by the rescinding party.

sections.heading: Other party need not perform
sections.body: On rescission, the other party need not perform any promise therein in which he is promisor.

sections.heading: Restore benefit
sections.body: Rescinding party shall restore any benefit received under the contract, so far as may be, to the person from whom it was received.

provisions.title: Consequences of rescission of voidable contract

examples.title: Rescission and restitution
examples.body: A’s consent was obtained by fraud. A rescinds. B need not perform further; A must restore any benefit received from B under s. 64.

hypotheticals.question: Can the rescinding party keep benefits already received?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 64 requires the rescinding party to restore such benefit, so far as may be, to the person from whom it was received.

misconceptions.trap: Rescission of a voidable contract leaves both parties free without any restitution duty.
misconceptions.correction: Section 64 requires the rescinding party to restore benefit received, so far as may be.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 64 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Establish valid rescission of a voidable contract. II. Apply non-performance by the other party. III. Apply restoration of benefit. IV. Conclude.

examTips: State both consequences: non-performance and restoration.
